I'm not familiar with Mint, just Debian and Ubuntu and Centos... but for a static IP, after the install, you modify the /etc/network/interfaces file with the proper IP and network gateway info.

Typically:

iface eth0 inet static

address 192.168.1.5

netmask 255.255.255.0

gateway 192.168.1.254

Using your info, of course,

Or for DHCP:

auto eth0

iface eth0 inet dhcp

If you don't need a static IP.

Remember to restart your network service after saving your work.

You can get automatic network configuration working by installing and starting/enabling NetworkManager.

As for Windows SMB networking compatibility, install samba and start/enable smbd and nmbd. Modify /etc/samba/smb.conf to contain:

[Share]

path = /path/to/your/share

public = yes

available = yes

browsable = yes

only guest = yes

writable = yes

You can download the latest version of Mint and boot with it. The system will start in a read only mode where nothing is saved to disk (I think everything is put on a ramdisk). Then you can see if you can get networking to work for you. The changes won't be saved and if it works, you'll need to do the install and then redo all the networking stuff.

Bottom line, don't be afraid to try. It shouldn't hurt anything.
